messages:
maria-cs: FYI customer reported ~500 users lost access after an Okta group rename last night. They say the SCIM sync ran with no errors but roles were removed from users that were only mapped via that Okta group. This looks like a group->role mapping gap, possibly externalId rotation. Need eng triage.

jordan-support: Customer tenant: acme-corp (tenant-id: t-9b1f). They did a group rename that triggered Okta to change group.externalId. Timing: 2026-02-14 02:14 UTC (Okta audit shows "Group renamed" event). SCIM connector shows a full group push at 02:15 UTC. They have a mapping: Okta Group -> Redwood Role (one-to-many groups allowed).

maria-cs: Repro summary from customer: after rename, users who were only members of that group lost the role and their access. They did a manual re-sync from Okta Admin and saw the group come back with a different externalId. They re-mapped the group in the Redwood Console and re-ran sync, which restored many users but ~12 users remained deprovisioned.

liam-eng: Can you paste the SCIM connector logs for the push? specifically the Group PATCH/PUT payload and our response codes. Also did the customer's provisioning token rotate around that time? If token scopes changed from scim:write to scim:read we'd see silent failures on mutating endpoints.

jordan-support: Pasted connector log snippet (redacted):

```
2026-02-14T02:15:12.345Z OKTA -> SCIM connector: PATCH /scim/v2/Groups/00g1XyzAbc123
payload: { "Operations": [{ "op": "replace", "path": "members", "value": [] }], "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"] }
2026-02-14T02:15:12.567Z SCIM <- connector: 204 No Content
2026-02-14T02:15:13.001Z OKTA audit: group.externalId changed from grp-ext-111 -> grp-ext-999
```

zara-ps: Interesting: OKTA sent a replace members with empty array? That would remove members if our server interpreted it literally. But they said the group rename caused externalId change; Okta might have created a new group behind the scenes and pushed a damage-control operation. If our mapping key is externalId, the new externalId won't match mapping -> our system might treat the group as unknown and apply a default removal policy. We should confirm our group handling logic on externalId/key mismatch.

liam-eng: @zara-ps yes.. two hypotheses: (A) Our import treats a PATCH on a group we don't recognize as "create+replace" which can lead to an empty members mutation on the canonical group record. (B) The connector used a rotated token with reduced scopes so mutations were accepted at HTTP layer (204) but ignored by internal auth layer. Need to check audit logs for internal auth errors.

maria-cs: I checked tenant audit in Redwood console: we have an event at 02:15:12 showing GroupPatch accepted. No explicit error. Admin console shows role mapping removed at 02:15:13 for role-id r-776.

liam-eng: Can we get a DB query to list users who lost role r-776 around that window? Also capture group records before/after.

zara-ps: Running a quick query against provisioning DB (read replica):

```
-- find users removed from role r-776 in 02:00-03:00 UTC
SELECT u.id, u.email, ar.role_id, ar.removed_at
FROM account_role ar
JOIN users u ON u.id = ar.user_id
WHERE ar.role_id = 'r-776' AND ar.removed_at BETWEEN '2026-02-14 02:00:00' AND '2026-02-14 03:00:00';
```

zara-ps: That returns 524 rows. 512 were re-added by manual sync, 12 still missing. I exported the 12 emails and sent to customer (they confirmed those accounts were flagged as "orphaned" in their Okta).

jordan-support: Customer claims those 12 users had identical email addresses but were deprovisioned earlier in Okta (Okta had deactivated them then reactivated with a new internal id). Could be Okta member id churn -> our dedupe by memberId failed.

liam-eng: Good point. We rely on Okta group member id (value in SCIM member object) + email fallback in some paths. If Okta removed and re-created the user (new id) and the group externalId also rotated, our merge logic might have detached the role. We need to check our idempotency keys for group membership ops.

maria-cs: Customer also shared an example SCIM user object before/after. Before: { "id": "00uOldId123", "userName": "jane.doe@acme.com" } After re-create: { "id": "00uNewId789", "userName": "jane.doe@acme.com" }

liam-eng: That matches churn. Two remediation paths: 1) Re-assign role to those 12 users in our Console (fast, manual). 2) Implement a backfill job that reconciles by email for recent churn window and re-applies roles if appropriate (safer for automated recovery). For immediate mitigation, we should run a targeted backfill for tenant t-9b1f for users with same email and role history within last 7 days.

sre-oncall: Also confirm connector token scopes and rotation: I queried secrets manager, provisioning-token for t-9b1f shows rotated at 2026-02-14T02:10:00Z and last rotation replaced full-scopes with a token labeled "scim:read write" (metadata shows correct). I don't see a scope downgrade to read-only. Okta-bot also shows a creation event at 02:10 for a new token.

okta-bot: Okta audit events:
```
2026-02-14T02:09:58Z INTEGRATION: API token created (id: tok-zzz)
2026-02-14T02:14:11Z GROUP: group renamed (id: 00g1XyzAbc123) name: "Engineering All" -> "Eng - All"
2026-02-14T02:14:12Z GROUP: group created (id: 00g1XNew456) externalId: grp-ext-999
```

liam-eng: Thanks. So token scopes look fine. Root cause likely combination of: Okta created a new group (new externalId) + re-created some users (new ids). Our group->role mapping key is externalId and our member patch semantics may have applied to the old group record. That resulted in removal and later re-add restored most users except cases where user id churn prevented automatic re-association.

maria-cs: Customer wants: (1) explanation of cause, (2) permanent fix to avoid this class of outage, (3) help restoring the 12 users programmatically.

liam-eng: ACTIONS: 
- (eng) I'll open an internal ticket to audit group patch handling & idempotency (ENG-PLAT-###). We should prefer stable mapping keys: support both externalId and displayName fuzzy match, and treat a PATCH for an unknown group as a create, not an update to an existing record.
- (ps) @zara-ps can you run a one-off backfill script for tenant t-9b1f to remap role r-776 for users with matching email and prior role history in last 7 days? Use a dry run first.
- (sre) @sre-oncall confirm if we need to throttle Okta full-sync events to avoid large replace ops.

zara-ps: I can run backfill. Sample pseudo-command I'll use (dry-run):

```
./scripts/scim_backfill --tenant t-9b1f --role r-776 --window 7d --match-by email --dry-run
```

zara-ps: Output (dry run) shows 12 matches, safe to reapply. I'll run live in 10m and report.

jordan-support: Customer approves manual reapply for the 12 users. They asked for a postmortem of root cause and an ETA for permanent fix. Please include mitigation guidance: don't bulk-rename Okta groups during business hours; prefer rename+preserve externalId or use Okta group profile attribute mapping.

liam-eng: For longer term fix: proposal: 1) Treat group mapping keys as triplet (externalId, oktaId, normalized displayName) and on mismatch attempt smart join before destructive ops. 2) Add a protective check: if PATCH replace members arrives and group identity can't be resolved, don't apply a destructive replace to any existing role memberships; instead create a pending delta and queue a reconciliation job. 3) Improve deprovision audit to record "source-event-id" so we can easily revert. I'll draft design and link in ENG ticket.

maria-cs: Thanks. @zara-ps please paste the final backfill result when done and confirm the 12 users were restored. Then I'll follow up with the customer and file a postmortem.

zara-ps: Live backfill completed at 02:45 UTC. Reapplied r-776 to 12 users. Logs: all 12 successfully re-granted. I'll attach run id and logs to the support case.

maria-cs: Customer acknowledged restore and requested we keep them posted on engineering fix ETA. I'll mark this high priority. :thumbsup:

liam-eng: I'll start a short RFC for the protective check and aim for a patch in next sprint. Assigning to eng-runtime to review SCIM op semantics.

sre-oncall: Noted. Will monitor any spikes in provisioning throughput as a follow-up.

maria-cs: Closing loop here for now. If anyone wants me to escalate to PM or Security for policy changes, ping me.

jordan-support: Thanks all — will update the customer thread and attach our remediation notes + recommended Okta best-practices.
